title: What the rules cost, where the records allow
question: What do the staffing and premium rules cost, and which cannot be priced from the records on disk?
finding: Overtime of the four fire suppression ranks that fill the fixed crews was $57.4 million in fiscal 2026 ($38.9 million in 2014; peak $75.4 million in fiscal 2022). Apparatus operator pay on the 261 driver and tiller positions is estimated at $2.0 million a year, $455,754 of it for 60 tiller positions; one seat around the clock on 20 trucks is about $10.5 million in base pay. 5 rules cannot be priced from the files on disk.
how: Payroll: the Controller's Employee Compensation file, Fire Department rows by job class. Estimates: positions on the Fire Department's 2026 vacancy list x the agreement's rate x the top step of the suppression firefighter scale (DHR pay-rate file) x the biweekly hours the agreement states x 26 pay periods a year (the Department of Human Resources Compensation Manual, fiscal 2026-27, prints H002 Firefighter at $5,960 biweekly and $154,960 a year, effective 7/1/2026: 154,960 / 5,960 = 26); seat cost uses the Budget and Legislative Analyst's posts-per-seat figure. Agreement-change costs are the Controller's own figures.
limits: Overtime of the suppression ranks also pays for vacancies, injuries, leave, strike-team deployments and events; it is not the cost of the crew rule alone. Estimates use base pay at the top step and leave out benefits, so the true figure may be higher or lower. The agreement provides that crews are set for the safety of members and the public, and the 2004 Controller review records reasons other cities give for five-member trucks.

rows.rule: Constant staffing of engines, trucks and squads (Fire 798 Unit 1, section 22)
rows.basis: Overtime paid in fiscal 2026 to the four suppression ranks that fill the crews (H-2, H-3, H-20, H-30): $57.4 million, against $38.9 million in fiscal 2014 (Controller payroll). Overtime also covers absences and vacancies, so this is the overtime of the ranks the rule governs, not of the rule alone.

rows.rule: Premiums of the same ranks (all kinds together)
rows.basis: "Other salaries" paid in fiscal 2026 to H-2, H-3, H-20 and H-30: $41.7 million. The payroll file does not split premiums by kind.
rows.record: Premium pay by earnings code and job class (Fire Department or Controller payroll extract) would give each premium separately.

rows.rule: At least five H-10 Incident Support Specialists on each watch (section 22.2)
rows.basis: Fiscal 2026: 12 payroll rows in class H-10 were paid $1.8 million in salaries and $847,288 in overtime (46% of salaries).

rows.rule: Apparatus operator pay, 5% (section 28): all driver and tiller positions on the 2026 vacancy list
rows.basis: Estimate: 261 FF/Driver and FF/Tiller positions on the Fire Department vacancy list (General Order 26 A-071) x 5% x top-step suppression firefighter base (59.9897 an hour x 97.4 hours x 26 pay periods = $151,918 a year, FY25-26). Base pay only; vacant positions, lower steps and relief operators move it either way.
rows.record: Payroll by earnings code (apparatus operator pay) would give the amount actually paid.

rows.basis: Same estimate for the 60 FF/Tiller positions on 20 trucks.

rows.rule: Fifth seat on every truck (section 22.1c sets one officer and four firefighters)
rows.basis: Estimate of what one seat around the clock costs across 20 trucks: 3.44 full-time posts per seat (Budget and Legislative Analyst, 2014) x 20 x $151,918 top-step base. Base salary only, no benefits or premiums.

rows.rule: Sixth seat on a truck whose aerial ladder is out of service (section 22.1c)
rows.basis: Cannot be computed: no file on disk says how many days each truck had an inoperative aerial ladder.
rows.record: Bureau of Equipment out-of-service log for aerial ladders, by truck and day.

rows.rule: Aerial ladder testing and recertification paid by the City (section 39.1)
rows.basis: Cannot be computed from the files on disk; the Fire Department budget books list ladder rebuilds but not testing.
rows.record: Central Shops / vendor invoices for aerial ladder testing.

rows.rule: Daily suppression minimum of 297 uniformed staff (Proposition F, Administrative Code 2A.97)
rows.basis: The Budget and Legislative Analyst (2014) put the daily minimum at 297 and the cost of a seat at 3.44 full-time posts; 297 x 3.44 = 1,022 posts before absences. No current daily-minimum figure is on disk.
rows.record: The Fire Department's current daily staffing minimum and relief factor.

rows.rule: Jail and court minimum staffing tables (Deputy Sheriffs, Appendix B)
rows.basis: Overtime cannot be tied to the table from the files on disk; the site’s “Pay by union and bargaining unit” page gives Sheriff overtime by unit. Sheriff overtime in fiscal 2026: $62.2 million, of which 77% in one unit (the site’s “Pay by union and bargaining unit” page).
rows.record: Sheriff post-by-post staffing and overtime by facility and shift.

rows.rule: Wooden ladder repair and construction by Central Shops
rows.basis: Cannot be computed: no file on disk prices the ladder shop.
rows.record: Central Shops budget or work orders for the ladder shop.

rows.basis: Controller cost letter on file 260355: added cost $0 in the first year shown and $9.9 million in the last.

rows.rule: Higher training and education pay (Fire 2026-2030 agreement)
rows.basis: Controller cost letter on file 260355: added cost $0 in the first year shown and $6.0 million in the last.

Board of Supervisors: labor agreement texts attached to the Board files that adopted them (Legistar)
